The extra typical bed-days metric shows how changes in typical length of stay and the number of admissions combine to create pressure on hospital capacity. Compared with 2014, stroke admissions in 2023 generated 1,659 additional typical bed-days—equivalent to about 4.5 extra beds occupied every day of the year. Heart attack admissions added a further 230 typical bed-days, making 1,889 across both event types. These estimates combine the change in median stay with annual event volume; they support service planning but do not measure actual bed occupancy.
